land.text: the Banate of Bosnia, raised to a kingdom when Tvrtko I was crowned in the fall of 1377 (probably 26 October)

predecessors.note: Tvrtko had ruled as ban since 1353 (S2); Cliopatria's banate row ends 1384 and the kingdom row begins 1385.

land.text: the kingdom's heartland, conquered by Mehmed II in May 1463 and organised as the Sanjak of Bosnia (Isa-beg first sanjakbey in 1464)

successors.note: Ottoman conquest: 25 May 1463 (infobox); S3 dates Isa-beg's sanjakbeyship to 1464.

land.text: Jajce and its fortress, retaken by Matthias on 26 December 1463 and made the Banate of Jajce

successors.note: Hungarian rule at Jajce lasted until 1527 (S1). The extent of the Banate of Jajce is not on the pages opened; a 40 km circle is a placeholder.

land.text: Hum, which Stjepan Vukcic Kosaca ruled as 'Herceg of Saint Sava' from 1448/49

successors.note: Cliopatria draws this land inside the Kingdom to 1481; the pages treat it as a separate duchy (Duchy of Saint Sava, infobox 1448-1482).

capitals.name: Bobovac
capitals.note: Infobox lists Visoko, Jajce and Bobovac without years; S1 calls Bobovac 'the chief royal residence' in the 1404 context and Visoko the seat where Tvrtko II retreated in 1432. Kraljeva Sutjeska, Mile and Milodraz were also court seats. Years are the researcher's span.

capitals.name: Jajce
capitals.note: Stephen Tomasevic was crowned at Jajce on 17 November 1461 (S4); S1 calls Jajce the capital of the 'all but completely annihilated kingdom' in 1463.

rulers.name: Tvrtko I
rulers.note: Infobox gives r. 1377-1391; the article body says 1353-91 counting his time as ban.

rulers.name: Tvrtko II
rulers.note: second reign; the infobox also lists Radivoj 1432-1435 and 1443-1446, overlapping, omitted from the strip

correction.text: Bosnia, Hum, the upper Drina and the Travunian coast as Tvrtko held them at his coronation; the 1385 outline is used unchanged for 1377-1384

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's kingdom row starts in 1385 but Tvrtko was crowned in 1377. The 1385 outline stands in for 1377-1384: S2 dates the 1373 gains (upper Podrinje, Gacko, part of Polimlje) and the early-1377 takeover of Trebinje, Konavli and Dracevica, all before the crown; Kotor and the Bay of Kotor (1382 fortress, 1385 recognition) are outside Cliopatria's outline.

52,419 km2 from 1385. S2 says Tvrtko 'enlarged the country's borders to their greatest extent' and styled himself king of Rascia, Bosnia, Dalmatia, Croatia and Pomorje in 1390; the Dalmatian towns and Klis (1387-1390) are not in the outline and are carried by ledger events. Neither page gives an area, so no infobox comparison is possible.
51,897 km2: two H3 cells (~500 km2) smaller than 1385 on the southern edge; no page opened explains it. Unverified: page budget.

51,327 km2: one cell less. S6: 'In 1399, the city [Ragusa] acquired the area between Ragusa and Pelješac' and a brief war with Bosnia in 1403-1404 'ended with Bosnian withdrawal'; the coastal strip is the ledger's 1399 loss.
49,910 km2: a few cells shift on the eastern edge (the outline now touches modern Serbia). No page opened dates it. Unverified: page budget.
49,650 km2: one cell less than 1415. Unverified: page budget.

Years only: the outline holds 1429-1447. From 1448 the Duchy of Saint Sava (infobox 'Established: 1448') holds Hum, so the Herzegovina part leaves the kingdom's shape; see the new keyframe 1448. The south edge moves north in 1429 because of Ragusa's Konavle purchases of 1419 and 1426 (S7). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1429..1447 from this entry's own 'valid for 1429-1447 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the kingdom without the Herzegovina of Herceg Stjepan, 1448-1452

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 1448 the Cliopatria kingdom outline minus Hum. S5: Stjepan Vukcic styled himself 'Herceg' from autumn 1448 and 'Herceg of Saint Sava' from the beginning of 1449; his lands were 'Hum, Primorje, Travunija, Onogost, Drina, Polimlje'. Whether the duke counted as a Bosnian vassal is not on the page; the two articles treat the states separately.

correction.text: the kingdom minus the Duchy of Saint Sava's Hum; valid 1453-1463 (the kingdom ends 25 May 1463)

keyframe_review.note: 49,412 km2 in Cliopatria; the correction removes Herzegovina (27 of the region's 34 cells lie inside the outline) as the Duchy's. The shape then holds to the fall of the kingdom in 1463.

correction.text: the adjusted 1453 shape for the kingdom's last year (to 25 May 1463); the 1463 Cliopatria outline (Herzegovina) is the Duchy of Saint Sava's

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts the outline to 8,134 km2 (Herzegovina) in 1463, but the kingdom 'fell in 1463' (infobox: Ottoman conquest 25 May 1463) and Herzegovina was Herceg Stjepan's duchy. The rump is therefore the Duchy's, not the kingdom's. For 1463 the kingdom is drawn with its adjusted 1453 shape; Hungary retook Jajce on 26 December 1463.

correction.text: Herzegovina: the Duchy of Saint Sava of Stjepan Vukcic's sons, not the kingdom; use the duchy's dossier

keyframe_review.note: No kingdom exists in 1468. The 8,134 km2 outline is Herzegovina, which S5 says the Ottomans conquered in the east in 1465 and which was 'much occupied by the Sanjak of Bosnia' by 1467; it belongs to duchy-of-saint-sava.

correction.text: Herzegovina and the Novi region: the duchy's last years to 1481, not the kingdom

keyframe_review.note: No kingdom exists in 1475. The 8,334 km2 outline is the remnant of the Duchy of Saint Sava under Vlatko Hercegovic (Ottoman vassal from 1470; Sanjak of Herzegovina formed 1470; last fortress Novi fell 1481).

region.text: Bosnia with Hum, the upper Drina and Travunia; 'the Serbs, Bosnia, Pomorje and the Western Areas'

ledger.note: 1377: Tvrtko I is crowned King of Bosnia at Mile. 'The coronation was held in the fall of 1377 (probably 26 October)', as 'king of the Serbs, Bosnia, Pomorje and the Western Areas'; S1 infobox 'lasted ... from 1377 to 1463'. The extent is Cliopatria's 1385 outline; the page names regions, not a boundary.

region.text: Kotor and the Bay of Kotor

ledger.note: 1385: the Hungarian queens recognise Tvrtko's possession of Kotor (spring); he had built a fortress in the Bay of Kotor in early 1382 (the later Novi). 'The queens recognized Tvrtko's possession of Kotor in the spring of 1385.'

region.text: Klis fortress and its district above Split

ledger.note: 1387: Tvrtko takes the Klis fortress. 'Tvrtko took control of the Klis Fortress in July 1387'; Ostrovica and Trogir followed. The page does not name the previous holder; the Hungarian crown (the queens) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities and islands that surrendered, with Klis and Trogir

ledger.note: 1390: the Dalmatian cities and islands surrender to Tvrtko, who styles himself 'king of Rascia, Bosnia, Dalmatia, Croatia, and Pomorje'. 'finally surrendered to Tvrtko in May 1390' (Split, Zadar and Sibenik were summoned in March 1389). Zadar is not included: S2 calls it 'the only Dalmatian city that had evaded his rule' (reviewer eu-18-f).

region.text: Kotor, Klis and the Dalmatian cities taken 1385-1390; the end of the hold is not on the page

ledger.note: 1391: bridging entry, page silent on when Tvrtko's Dalmatian and Kotor acquisitions ended. The date is Tvrtko's death on 10 March 1391, the last date S2 gives for his Dalmatian title; the outline of Cliopatria's 1395 shape does not include them.

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1399: Ragusa acquires the coast between the city and Pelješac. 'In 1399, the city acquired the area between Ragusa and Pelješac.' The page does not name the seller; Bosnia is the researcher's reading from the 1403-1404 Bosnian war over it.

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1403: Bosnia and Ragusa go to war. 'A brief war with Bosnia in 1403 and 1404 ended with Bosnian withdrawal.'

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1404: the war ends with the Bosnian withdrawal; Ragusa keeps the strip.

1419: Sandalj Hranic sells eastern Konavle to Ragusa. 'on June 24, 1419, by a purchase and sale agreement'; S7 says Konavle was 'part of Bosnia in the hands of powerful feudal lords' at the start of the century. The seller was a Bosnian magnate, the researcher reads the land as the kingdom's.

region.text: the western part of Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod

ledger.note: 1426: Ragusa buys the rest of Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod, from Radoslav Pavlovic. 'on December 31, 1426, the Ragusans purchased the remaining western part of Konavle'.

region.text: Hum, Primorje, Travunija, Onogost, Drina, Polimlje

ledger.note: 1448: Stjepan Vukcic becomes 'Herceg of Saint Sava' and Hum leaves the kingdom's drawn shape. 'Since the autumn of 1448, he started to style himself as Herceg ... from the beginning of 1449 ... Herceg of Saint Sava'; infobox 'Established: 1448'. Year set to 1448 to match the 1448 keyframe and the duchy's found event (infobox 'Established: 1448'; reviewer eu-18-f).

region.text: the kingdom's heartland, Ottoman after May 1463; Jajce Hungarian from December

ledger.note: 1463: Mehmed II conquers Bosnia and has King Stephen Tomasevic beheaded on 25 May. 'In May 1463, Mehmed marched into Bosnia, meeting little effective resistance, and captured Stephen, who was then beheaded' (infobox 'Died: 25 May 1463 ... Jajce'); the heartland becomes the Sanjak of Bosnia (Isa-beg sanjakbey in 1464, S3). Matthias of Hungary retakes Jajce on 26 December 1463 (S1).

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Bosnia
wars.outcome: The Ottomans raided eastern Bosnia from 1384 and attacked the kingdom from about 1386; the conquest ended in May 1463 with the execution of Stephen Tomasevic.
wars.note: S1 dates 'the first Ottoman troops attacked Bosnia in May 1414' and Ottoman suzerainty with annual tribute in 1425; S3 says raids from 1384, attacks from 1386, the Bosnian Krajiste march in 1451. The tribute relation belongs in the Ottoman dossier as a vassal_start with counterpart kingdom-of-bosnia.

wars.name: Ragusan-Bosnian war of 1403-1404

zones.text: the strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

wars.outcome: 'ended with Bosnian withdrawal'; Ragusa kept the area it acquired in 1399.

wars.name: Hungarian-Bosnian conflict of 1404
wars.outcome: 'in June 1404, Tvrtko's supporters defeated a Hungarian army and thus prevented Ostoja from reclaiming the crown'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Siege of Jajce (1463)
wars.outcome: Jajce 'was captured by Hungarians under Matthias on 26 December 1463' and became the Banate of Jajce, which resisted until 1527.

certainty.note: Medieval Bosnia's frontiers are approximate throughout; the Ragusan frontier is the exception once Konavle was bought (1419 and 1426), but it is outside the kingdom's drawn shape.

notes:
Failed pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banate_of_Jajce, /Jajce_Banovina and /Banate_of_Jajce_(1463) (url_not_found); the Banate of Jajce (Hungarian, 1463-1527) is therefore only a note in the successors and in the Siege of Jajce war, with a 40 km placeholder circle. A gap-filler should find the article's real title.
Overlap with the Duchy of Saint Sava: Cliopatria keeps Hum inside the kingdom to 1481 and draws a small 2,778 km2 'Duchy of Saint Sava' in the Montenegrin interior; the pages opened treat the Duchy (Stjepan Vukcic, infobox 1448-1482, capital Blagaj) as a separate state, so this dossier removes Herzegovina from the kingdom from 1448 and calls Cliopatria's 1463-1481 rump (8,134 km2, 23 of 30 cells inside Herzegovina) the duchy's. The Kingdom page itself still speaks of Herzegovina as Bosnia's remnant; the nominal vassalage of Herceg Stjepan to the Bosnian crown is not on any page opened.
Not on the pages: the 'annexed portions of eastern Bosnia in the 1440s and 1450s' (S1) has no place or year, so there is no event (the Cliopatria shape does not drop any eastern land); the Cliopatria shape changes of 1395, 1415, 1422 are 1-5 cells each and unexplained; the end of Tvrtko's Dalmatian and Kotor gains (ledger 1391 at confidence 1). The Ottoman tribute from 1425 and the Hungarian Banate of Jajce need events in the ottoman-empire and kingdom-of-hungary dossiers (counterpart kingdom-of-bosnia).
Gazetteer names needed: Konavle, Primorje (Dubrovnik littoral), Pelješac, Klis, Jajce, Bobovac, Visoko, Mile, Kraljeva Sutjeska (places/regions); coordinates here are placeholders at map scale. Infobox area: none on S1 or S2.
